# Legacy AI — full content

> Legacy AI builds and runs pre-built AI systems for owner-operated businesses across Indiana — phone answering, lead follow-up, scheduling, reviews, reporting and customer records. 54 productized solutions, already in production. One call. One person. One bill.

Legacy AI is led by founder Douglas Talley and based in Brown County, Indiana. Everything offered is already built and already in production for businesses such as an auto body shop in Bloomington, a plumber's office in Nashville, a chiropractor in Columbus, and a property inspection company covering every county in Indiana.

## How engagements work
1. You tell us what's broken — describe the pain points on a 30-minute call. No pitch.
2. We agree on the plan — scope, price and timeline in writing before work begins. Most projects begin with a deposit; for service trades, advertising exchanges or combined arrangements, the value and commitments are agreed up front.
3. We build. You see it working — configuration, customization and testing, then a walkthrough with your branding and workflow. One session.
4. We go live together — launch and put it to work. Payments follow the agreed schedule, with milestones for larger projects. Day one.
5. We keep making it better — monthly reports, quarterly reviews, ongoing improvements.

## Industries already served
Auto body & collision; plumbers, HVAC and contractors; chiropractic & wellness; restaurants & hospitality; professional services; property inspection. If your business has customers, Legacy AI can build for it.

## The 54 solutions
- The Silent Closer (Web · 24/7): A friendly conversation on your website answers questions about prices, hours and services, then books the appointment. It works around the clock, even at two in the morning.
- The Receptionist Who Never Calls In (Voice · Bilingual): A real-sounding voice answers calls, handles questions and books appointments directly into your calendar. Spanish-language conversations help customers who might otherwise hang up find their way to a booking.
- The Live Booking Calendar (Scheduling): Customers choose a time on your website without phone tag. The calendar checks your actual availability, so it only offers open slots and avoids double-bookings.
- The Daily Hunter (Outbound · Nightly): Automated local prospecting looks for people in your area who need what you sell. It runs daily, bringing opportunities to your business without a morning of dialing.
- The Lead Catcher (Lead Capture): Capture who a visitor is and what they wanted, even when they leave before finishing the form. Follow up on the interest that might otherwise disappear.
- The Missed-Call Recovery (SMS · Auto): When you cannot answer, the caller gets a friendly text back instantly. Keep the conversation open and give missed calls another path to becoming booked work.
- The Follow-Up Machine (Nurture): Text each new lead, nudge outstanding quotes and ask for reviews at the right moment. Follow-up keeps moving without becoming another task on your desk.
- The Traffic Tattletale (Analytics): See where customers came from, what they clicked and what prompted their call. Use that view to understand which advertising is earning its place.
- The Review Harvester (Reviews · Auto): Send a gentle review request after a good experience, on the platform that matters to your business. Customer concerns go to you first so you can address the problem.
- The Report Writer (Field → Report): A technician captures photos, measurements and findings by speaking into a phone at the job site. That information becomes a branded report delivered to the customer, before the trip back is over.
- The Talk-To-Type Field Tool (Voice Entry): Crews speak instead of typing on small screens. The tool records conditions, materials and measurements so field notes move faster and the important details get written down.
- The Technician Dashboard (Workflow): Guide every technician through the same sequence: en route, on site, working and done. Required steps and before photos stay part of the job, rather than something someone remembers later.
- The Digital Sign-Off (Paperless): The customer signs on the phone. Approval is recorded and filed in seconds, without a paper form to chase or a promise to send it later.
- On-Site Card Processing (Payments): Take a card payment at the customer's property and send a branded receipt straight to their inbox. Finish the payment while you are still on site.
- The Upsell Menu (Revenue): Show the standard service alongside optional extras on the same screen. Customers can add the work they want, giving each job room to grow without a hard sell.
- The Invoice Chaser (Collections): Unpaid invoices receive polite, persistent follow-up until they are paid. The reminders keep moving without relying on your memory or putting you in the chasing role.
- Books That Balance Themselves (Accounting): Payments, receipts and expenses are sorted and categorized for your accountant. Keep the records ready throughout the year so April does not begin with a scramble.
- The Dispatcher (Dispatch): Match each call with the technician who is nearby, available and equipped with the right truck. Coordinate the job without a whiteboard, group text or another dispatch call to you.
- A Real Custom Website (Website): A custom site built for your trade, your town and your customers. Designed from scratch and fast on phones, it gives your business a polished presence that earns its keep.
- High-Converting Landing Pages (Conversion): A focused page turns a campaign click into a phone call. Built in a day for a seasonal promotion or an ad, then tuned to improve the response.
- Website Rescue (Rescue): We take over a slow or broken website, fix the problems and make it fast. You keep your domain and get a site you can feel comfortable sending customers to.
- The Customer Portal (Deliverables): Give customers clean, secure links to their reports, videos and invoices. A clear delivery experience makes finding the finished work feel as straightforward as tracking a package.
- A Page For Every Neighborhood (SEO · Programmatic): Create a page for every city, town and ZIP code you serve, written with local landmarks and local language. This approach is already in production for a statewide Indiana service business.
- Top Of Google For Your Town (SEO): Improve your visibility for your trade in your area with useful content and sound site structure. Help neighbors find your business when they search for the service you provide.
- Get Recommended By ChatGPT (GEO · AI Answers): Build your business's presence in answers from ChatGPT and other AI assistants. When someone asks for a local recommendation, your business is prepared to be part of the conversation.
- The Map Pack (Local · Maps): Manage your Google Business profile with current posts, photos and reviews, supporting visibility in the top three Google Maps results for nearby searches.
- The Review Ladder (Reviews): Automatically ask happy customers for a review at a moment when the experience is fresh. Build the reputation that supports stronger, lasting visibility in local search.
- Bad-Review Interception (Reviews · Triage): Route unhappy customers to you first so you can resolve their concerns before they become a public review. Give a difficult experience a better ending.
- Review Response Handling (Engagement): Every review, positive or negative, gets a thoughtful response in your brand's voice within the day. Customers see a business that is attentive without you logging in to reply.
- Social Proof Everywhere (Social Proof): Put your strongest reviews to work on your website, landing pages, ads and follow-up emails. Let customers hear from the people who have already chosen you.
- The Writer Who Never Sleeps (Content): Articles, blog posts, service pages and newsletters, all in your voice. The existing client workflow produces more than 800 pieces a year with about an hour a week of the client's attention.
- The Social Media Sidekick (Social): Keep posts on schedule, the feed active and comments answered. Stay familiar to your audience without opening Instagram while you are on a job.
- Long-To-Short Video (Video · Repurpose): Turn one job-site video into twenty short clips for TikTok, Reels and YouTube Shorts. Captions and hooks are included, giving one filming session a month of posts.
- Blog From A Voice Memo (Voice-First): A ten-minute voice memo about a job becomes a blog post, an email and five social posts. Capture what you know from the truck without sitting down at a keyboard.
- Done-For-You Ad Campaigns (Ads): Campaigns for Google, Facebook, Instagram and local directories. We handle creative, copy, targeting and ongoing tuning so you can focus on answering the inquiries.
- Email & Text Campaigns (Email · SMS): Newsletters, promotions, seasonal reminders and messages to win back quiet customers. Written in your voice and sent when they are relevant to the people on your list.
- Seasonal Automation (Automation): Schedule spring tune-ups, pre-winter check-ups, back-to-school specials and other recurring reminders. The right message returns each year without another calendar task.
- Sales Outreach On Autopilot (Prospecting): Find and research prospects, prepare a personal-sounding message and send it. Interesting replies come to you, keeping outreach moving while you do the work.
- The Quote-From-Photo Tool (Quoting): A customer texts a photo of a dented fender, leaky pipe or cracked driveway and receives a ballpark quote in about sixty seconds. Make the next step toward booking simple.
- The Q&A Specialist (Support): Answer the questions customers ask most often, all day, in your voice. Unusual questions are escalated to you so your time goes to the conversations that need you.
- Outbound Reminder Calls (Outbound): Appointment confirmations, follow-ups and review requests delivered in a real-sounding voice. Complete the calls you rarely have time to make yourself.
- Multilingual Customer Capture (Bilingual): Bilingual conversations and booking help Spanish-speaking customers get past the voicemail barrier. A full translation is handed to you for the next step.
- Locked Doors On Your Website (Security): Protect the front door of your website by blocking attacks and unwanted bots. The setup addresses eighty common ways attackers get in, reducing avoidable exposure.
- Backups That Actually Work (Backups): Customer information, job records, photos and reports are backed up automatically, encrypted and recoverable. A failed laptop or hard drive does not have to take the records with it.
- Lawyer-Proof Setup (Compliance): Put privacy policies, data handling rules and deletion rights into your setup. Organize how customer information is handled and reduce the gaps that can turn into expensive problems.
- Disaster Recovery Plan (Recovery): Give each system a written recovery plan. When a fire, flood or other disruption happens, there is a clear route back to work rather than a plan to invent under pressure.
- The Owner's Dashboard (Dashboard): Bring leads, jobs, revenue, top services and customer sources onto one clear screen. See the numbers you need without digging through an analytics tool.
- Where The Money Came From (Attribution): Connect advertising spend to booked jobs and revenue. Understand which marketing activity produces work so you can make informed decisions about the next dollar.
- Competitor Watch (Intelligence): Follow competitors' search rankings, prices, ads and reviews as they change. Keep the information current so changes in your market do not arrive as a surprise.
- Sales Alerts On Your Phone (Alerts): Get a phone alert when a real prospect arrives on your site or a payment reaches your account. Stay in the loop without living in your inbox.
- Subscription Bloat Audit (Audit): Review recurring account charges and flag services you no longer need. Most clients find savings on the first pass that cover the audit fee.
- Make Your Tools Talk (Integration): Connect your calendar, email, accounting, field app and customer list. Enter a customer once and move the details between the systems automatically.
- Move Off The System You Hate (Migration): Move customers, history and files out of the software that no longer fits. Settle into a system built around the way your business actually works.
- Customer List That Actually Works (CRM): Set up your customer list properly and load the records you already have. Replace fragile spreadsheets with an organized system your business can use.
